rules.subject: landside
rules.rationale: The public landside and the restricted airside are separate zones with no door between them; the only way across is through security screening.

rules.subject: airside
rules.rationale: A departing passenger on the landside reaches the airside and the gates only by passing security screening, which is the single choke point of that route.
exceptions: Staff and crew use separate controlled entries
Transfer passengers arriving airside have their own arrangements

rules.subject: check_in
rules.rationale: Check-in is on the landside, in the departures hall, and passengers reach it before they reach security screening.
exceptions: Off-airport or remote check-in, which leaves only bag drop

rules.subject: departures_hall
rules.rationale: The departures hall is next to the kerb where passengers are dropped off, so they come in with their bags by the shortest way.
exceptions: Terminals reached by rail or by a transit link

rules.subject: arrivals_route
rules.rationale: Arriving passengers, who have not been screened, never share a route with departing ones on the airside, and their landside routes do not cross.
exceptions: Small terminals sharing one hall and managing the flows by time

rules.subject: international_arrivals
rules.rationale: An arriving international passenger passes immigration first, and only then reaches the baggage reclaim and the landside.
exceptions: Preclearance or transit arrivals handled elsewhere

rules.subject: customs
rules.rationale: Customs comes after the baggage reclaim, because a passenger must have their bags before they can be inspected.
exceptions: Hand-baggage-only passengers who skip the reclaim

rules.subject: baggage_reclaim
rules.rationale: The baggage reclaim sits beside the arrivals hall, where passengers leave the secured area for the public landside.

rules.subject: baggage_handling
rules.rationale: Bags tagged at check-in drop onto the sortation system directly behind the counters, so the landside bag path is short. Its relation to the make-up area is open, see the conflict ledger.
exceptions: Remote bag halls linked by long conveyors

rules.subject: baggage_makeup
rules.rationale: The make-up area, where bags are sorted to flights, is close to the apron, so bags travel a short enclosed route to the aircraft, and it is back-of-house.
exceptions: Remote bag halls or off-airport sorting

rules.subject: baggage_makeup
rules.rationale: Checked bags are screened before they reach the make-up area, so no unscreened bag is loaded.

rules.subject: gate
rules.rationale: Every gate opens onto the airside concourse, so passengers walk from security to their gate along one connected route.
exceptions: Bus gates reached from a ground-level lounge

rules.subject: concessions
rules.rationale: Shops and food are airside, on the walk between security and the gates, so passengers who have been screened can use them before they board.
exceptions: Landside shops for meeters and greeters

rules.subject: staff_entry
rules.rationale: Staff and crew have their own entry and screening, and their routes do not cross the passenger routes of the airside.

rules.subject: apron_access
rules.rationale: The apron and the aircraft are reached from the airside only, never straight from a landside space.

rules.subject: international_pier
rules.rationale: International and domestic passengers are kept on separate piers or levels, so passengers who have been through border control do not mix with those who have not.
exceptions: Flexible gates swing between the two uses

conflicts.topic: Which side of the screening is which

positions.position: Security screening is reached only through the landside (confidence 0.98).
The airside is reached only through security screening (confidence 0.9).
The checkpoint is reached only through the airside, though its rationale calls it the single gateway between landside and airside (confidence 0.95).

conflicts.resolution: The direction is landside, then screening, then airside. The haiku predicate runs the wrong way and its own rationale disagrees with it, so it is not adopted.

positions.position: The make-up area close to the apron (confidence 0.7).

conflicts.resolution: Both are kept as separate rules. They are compatible if the system is two spaces joined by a conveyor, and a rule pack that models it as one space cannot meet both.
